pages.text: Teotihuacan is a very old city in Mexico. It is located about forty kilometers northeast of modern Mexico City. This place is famous for its large and important pyramids built long before the Aztec Empire existed.
pages.caption: Front view of the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Teotihuacan Sun Front.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Front view of the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: The city had many people living in it. At its highest point, it was one of the largest cities in the world. People lived in special multi-family houses and walked along the wide Avenue of the Dead.
pages.caption: Left side view of the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Pyramid of the sun teotihuacan with crowd.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Left side view of the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: The early history of the city is quite mysterious. People do not know exactly who founded it. Later, the Aztecs found these great ruins and named the place Teotihuacan, which means birthplace of the gods.
pages.caption: View of the Pyramid of the Moon from the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Piramide de la Luna 072006.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: View of the Pyramid of the Moon from the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: The city had no major military walls or structures. Scholars debate how the city was ruled because they have not found records of kings. Many believe that the people used a form of collective governance.
pages.caption: Platform along the Avenue of the Dead showing the talud-tablero architectural style

evidence.fileTitle: File:MW-Teotihuacan8.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Platform along the Avenue of the Dead showing the talud-tablero architectural style

pages.text: Later on, major monuments were burned and destroyed. Scholars used to think foreign invaders attacked the city. Now, new evidence suggests the destruction might have been caused by an internal uprising.

B1-B2.headline: Exploring the Ancient Metropolis of Teotihuacan

pages.text: Located in a sub-valley of the Valley of Mexico, Teotihuacan was an ancient Mesoamerican city situated forty kilometers northeast of modern-day Mexico City. It is widely known today for its architecturally significant pyramids, including the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, which predated the Aztec Empire by many centuries.
pages.caption: Front view of the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Teotihuacan Sun Front.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Front view of the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: At its zenith, Teotihuacan was the largest city in the Americas, with an estimated population ranging from 25,000 to over 100,000 people. The city covered twenty-one square kilometers and featured complex multi-family residential compounds, vibrant murals, and an extensive export network for fine obsidian tools.
pages.caption: Left side view of the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Pyramid of the sun teotihuacan with crowd.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Left side view of the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: The exact ethnicity of the inhabitants and the identity of the city's founders remain subjects of ongoing debate among scholars. Some suggest the population was multi-ethnic, consisting of migrants from various regions across Mesoamerica who were drawn to the thriving urban center.
pages.caption: View of the Pyramid of the Moon from the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Piramide de la Luna 072006.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: View of the Pyramid of the Moon from the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: Unlike many contemporaneous cities in the region, Teotihuacan lacks striking evidence of a king or authoritarian ruler, such as royal palaces or war depictions. Because of this absence, many scholars have concluded that the city relied on some form of collective governance rather than dynastic rule.
pages.caption: Platform along the Avenue of the Dead showing the talud-tablero architectural style

evidence.fileTitle: File:MW-Teotihuacan8.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Platform along the Avenue of the Dead showing the talud-tablero architectural style

pages.text: Around 550 CE, the major monuments of the city were systematically burned and sacked. While earlier scholars assumed foreign invaders were responsible, recent evidence indicates the burning was concentrated on major civic structures, suggesting it may have stemmed from an internal uprising.

Centuries after the collapse of the city, Nahua migrants repopulated the area. When the later Aztecs encountered the magnificent ruins, they claimed a common ancestry with the original inhabitants and adopted various aspects of their culture and religious traditions.

Situated in the Valley of Mexico forty kilometers northeast of modern-day Mexico City, Teotihuacan stands as one of the pre-Columbian Americas' most prominent ancient urban centers. Famous for monumental structures like the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, the settlement flourished long before the rise of the Aztec Empire.
pages.caption: Front view of the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Teotihuacan Sun Front.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Front view of the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: During its demographic peak in the first half of the first millennium, the city encompassed twenty-one square kilometers and housed a vast population. Archaeological remains reveal sophisticated multi-family residential compounds, well-preserved murals, the Avenue of the Dead, and a far-reaching trade network centered on obsidian tool exportation.
pages.caption: Left side view of the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Pyramid of the sun teotihuacan with crowd.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Left side view of the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: The precise ethnicity of Teotihuacan's populace and the origin of its founders continue to generate scholarly debate. Hypotheses range from specific linguistic groups such as Nahuas, Otomi, or Totonac to a decidedly multi-ethnic populace drawing migrants from Oaxaca, the Gulf Coast, and the Maya region.
pages.caption: View of the Pyramid of the Moon from the Pyramid of the Sun

evidence.fileTitle: File:Piramide de la Luna 072006.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: View of the Pyramid of the Moon from the Pyramid of the Sun

pages.text: A notable absence of dynastic markers distinguishes Teotihuacan from contemporaneous Mesoamerican polities. The lack of royal palaces, ceremonial ball courts, and artistic depictions of warfare and captive humiliation has led numerous researchers to theorize that the city operated under a system of collective governance.
pages.caption: Platform along the Avenue of the Dead showing the talud-tablero architectural style

evidence.fileTitle: File:MW-Teotihuacan8.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Platform along the Avenue of the Dead showing the talud-tablero architectural style

pages.text: Around 550 CE, major civic structures along the Avenue of the Dead experienced systematic burning and destruction. While initial archaeological interpretations attributed this devastation to foreign invasion, contemporary evaluations suggest the damage was primarily restricted to upper-class structures, pointing toward a possible internal sociopolitical uprising.

Long after the metropolis fell into abandonment, later Nahua groups repopulated the surrounding area. Upon encountering the monumental ruins, the Aztecs integrated aspects of Teotihuacano heritage into their own cosmological framework, interpreting the site as the mythical birthplace of the gods.

title: The Mission and History of Public Health
attribution: Adapted from English Wikipedia contributors; see pinned revision and history. SAGA AI-assisted adaptation under CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikipedia does not endorse SAGA.

pages.text: Public health is about keeping people healthy and stopping diseases before they start. It helps groups of people, from small towns to entire cities, live longer and better lives by focusing on physical and mental well-being.
pages.caption: A community health worker in Korail Basti, a slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh

imageProvenance.credit: DFID - UK Department for International Development

evidence.fileTitle: File:A community health worker conducting a survey in the Korail slum, Bangladesh (8630810827).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A community health worker in Korail Basti, a slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: This big field uses many tools to help communities. Experts look at health data, teach people about good habits, give vaccines, and make sure drinking water is clean and safe for everyone.
pages.caption: The WHO is the predominant agency associated with global health.

evidence.fileTitle: File:World Health Organisation building from west.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: The WHO is the predominant agency associated with global health.

pages.text: In the past, growing cities needed new ways to fight illness. Great Britain became a leader in public health by building better sewer systems and working hard to control dangerous infectious diseases.
pages.caption: A Public Health Prayer - Dr Edmond Fernandes

evidence.fileTitle: File:Public Health Prayer by Dr Edmond Fernandes.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A Public Health Prayer - Dr Edmond Fernandes

pages.text: Today, public health also deals with long-term sickness like heart disease and cancer. Groups like the World Health Organization work hard around the world to stop sickness and help people stay healthy.
pages.caption: A Somali boy is injected with inactivated poliovirus vaccine (Mogadishu, 1993).

evidence.fileTitle: File:Somali boy receives a polio vaccination.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A Somali boy is injected with inactivated poliovirus vaccine (Mogadishu, 1993).

pages.text: Poor countries still face big challenges because they often lack trained workers and money. Even with these difficulties, public health programs continue to save lives and protect communities everywhere.

B1-B2.headline: The Mission and History of Public Health

pages.text: Public health is the science and art of preventing disease, prolonging life, and promoting well-being through organized societal efforts. It analyzes population health threats, addressing physical, psychological, and social factors for groups ranging from small communities to entire continents.
pages.caption: A community health worker in Korail Basti, a slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh

imageProvenance.credit: DFID - UK Department for International Development

evidence.fileTitle: File:A community health worker conducting a survey in the Korail slum, Bangladesh (8630810827).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A community health worker in Korail Basti, a slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: As an interdisciplinary field, public health covers environmental health, biostatistics, and public policy. Practical initiatives include vaccination delivery, air quality promotion, hand-washing education, and programs to prevent suicide and reduce smoking.
pages.caption: The WHO is the predominant agency associated with global health.

evidence.fileTitle: File:World Health Organisation building from west.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: The WHO is the predominant agency associated with global health.

pages.text: Historical public health efforts emerged in Great Britain during the nineteenth century because it was the first modern urban nation. Rapid urbanization created health distress, leading to vital sanitation projects like sewerage systems, alongside quarantine measures and scientific progress.
pages.caption: A Public Health Prayer - Dr Edmond Fernandes

evidence.fileTitle: File:Public Health Prayer by Dr Edmond Fernandes.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A Public Health Prayer - Dr Edmond Fernandes

pages.text: As infectious diseases decreased through the twentieth century, public health priorities shifted toward chronic illnesses like cancer and heart disease. Meanwhile, global organizations like the World Health Organization tackle major health emergencies and coordinate international disease eradication.
pages.caption: A Somali boy is injected with inactivated poliovirus vaccine (Mogadishu, 1993).

evidence.fileTitle: File:Somali boy receives a polio vaccination.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A Somali boy is injected with inactivated poliovirus vaccine (Mogadishu, 1993).

pages.text: Significant disparities persist between developed and developing nations, where limited financial resources and shortages of trained workers hinder medical care. Furthermore, certain interventions remain controversial, sparking debates regarding personal freedom versus government responsibility in shaping health policies.

C1-C2.headline: Global Frameworks and Evolution of Public Health

pages.text: Public health encompasses the collective science and organized efforts aimed at preventing disease, extending life expectancy, and enhancing societal well-being. By analyzing population-level determinants and health threats, it addresses physical, psychological, and social health parameters across scales ranging from local communities to global populations.
pages.caption: A community health worker in Korail Basti, a slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh

imageProvenance.credit: DFID - UK Department for International Development

evidence.fileTitle: File:A community health worker conducting a survey in the Korail slum, Bangladesh (8630810827).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A community health worker in Korail Basti, a slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: Operating as a multi-faceted interdisciplinary domain, public health integrates epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, and health economics. Implementation occurs through systematic case surveillance, promotion of healthy behaviors, vaccination distribution, and environmental interventions designed to mitigate risks.
pages.caption: The WHO is the predominant agency associated with global health.

evidence.fileTitle: File:World Health Organisation building from west.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: The WHO is the predominant agency associated with global health.

pages.text: Historically, Great Britain pioneered modern public health frameworks during the nineteenth century in response to urban distress. Driven by rapid industrialization, initial strategies prioritized sanitation infrastructure, infectious disease containment via quarantine and vaccination, and the application of emerging scientific disciplines.
pages.caption: A Public Health Prayer - Dr Edmond Fernandes

evidence.fileTitle: File:Public Health Prayer by Dr Edmond Fernandes.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A Public Health Prayer - Dr Edmond Fernandes

pages.text: Following the epidemiological transition and the subsequent decline of infectious diseases in the twentieth century, public health mandates pivoted toward chronic conditions such as cardiovascular disease and malignancies. Concurrently, the World Health Organization directs international responses to health emergencies and coordinates global disease eradication campaigns.
pages.caption: A Somali boy is injected with inactivated poliovirus vaccine (Mogadishu, 1993).

evidence.fileTitle: File:Somali boy receives a polio vaccination.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: A Somali boy is injected with inactivated poliovirus vaccine (Mogadishu, 1993).

pages.text: Profound disparities in infrastructure and resource allocation separate developed regions from developing nations, where maternal and child health challenges remain acute. Moreover, utilitarian public health interventions frequently generate ethical dilemmas, balancing population-level risk mitigation against individual autonomy and personal liberties.

title: Global Resistance Against Fascism
attribution: Adapted from English Wikipedia contributors; see pinned revision and history. SAGA AI-assisted adaptation under CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikipedia does not endorse SAGA.

pages.text: Anti-fascism is a political movement that opposes fascist groups, ideas, and individuals. It began in Europe during the 1920s. The movement grew very strong shortly before and during World War II. During the war, many countries and resistance groups fought against the Axis powers.
pages.caption: Hitler with Mussolini at the site of the 20 July Plot, an attempted bombing assassination of Hitler by dissident German military officers that took place in 1944

imageProvenance.credit: Unknown authorUnknown author Unknown authorUnknown author

evidence.fileTitle: File:Bundesarchiv Bild 146-1969-071A-03, Hitler-Attentat vom 20. Juli 1944.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Hitler with Mussolini at the site of the 20 July Plot, an attempted bombing assassination of Hitler by dissident German military officers that took place in 1944

pages.text: Before World War II, many Western nations did not take the threat of fascism very seriously. Sometimes, people even associated anti-fascism with communism. However, the start of World War II changed these views completely. Fascism came to be seen as a huge danger by the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union.
pages.caption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

evidence.fileTitle: File:FDR-1944-Campaign-Portrait (retouched, cropped) (1).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

pages.text: Anti-fascist movements first started in Italy when Benito Mussolini rose to power. Soon, these movements spread to other European countries and then across the entire world. In the early days, people from many different political backgrounds worked together to oppose fascism.
pages.caption: Winston Churchill

evidence.fileTitle: File:Sir Winston Churchill - 19086236948.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Winston Churchill

pages.text: In Italy, Mussolini used a secret police force to stop his opponents. During the 1920s, anti-fascist workers fought against Mussolini and his violent Blackshirts. When some trade unions made peace agreements, other workers formed groups like Arditi del Popolo to keep fighting.
pages.caption: Charles de Gaulle

evidence.articleCaption: Charles de Gaulle

pages.text: After World War II ended, anti-fascist movements continued in places where fascism tried to return. In Germany and the United States, antifa groups grew during the 1980s and 1990s, often supported by punk music scenes. In the 21st century, these groups grew even more to fight against the radical right.

Anti-fascism is a political movement that opposes fascist ideologies, groups, and individuals. Originating in Europe during the 1920s, it reached its greatest significance shortly before and during World War II. During this conflict, the Axis powers were opposed by numerous allied nations and dozens of global resistance movements.

pages.text: Before World War II, Western countries largely failed to take the threat of fascism seriously, and anti-fascism was sometimes linked with communism. However, the outbreak of the war fundamentally altered Western perceptions. Fascism was suddenly viewed as an existential threat not only by the Soviet Union, but also by the democratic United States and United Kingdom.
pages.caption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

evidence.fileTitle: File:FDR-1944-Campaign-Portrait (retouched, cropped) (1).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

pages.text: Anti-fascist movements emerged initially in Italy during the rise of Benito Mussolini before spreading globally. The early period involved communist, socialist, anarchist, and Christian-democratic organizers. Until 1928, there was significant collaboration between communist and non-communist anti-fascists.
pages.caption: Winston Churchill

evidence.fileTitle: File:Sir Winston Churchill - 19086236948.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Winston Churchill

pages.text: In Italy, Mussolini's regime labeled its opponents as anti-fascists and established a secret police force for repression. Throughout the 1920s, anti-fascists fought against violent Blackshirts and Mussolini's rise. When some labor groups adopted pacified strategies, dissenting workers formed groups like Arditi del Popolo to continue the fight.
pages.caption: Charles de Gaulle

imageProvenance.credit: Office of War Information, Overseas Picture Division. [1] The image prefix (LC-USW3) at the Library of Congress image page matches that of pictures from the OWI collection (see prefix list here.

pages.text: Following World War II, the movement remained active wherever organized fascism re-emerged. A resurgence of antifa occurred in Germany during the 1980s in response to neo-Nazis infiltrating the punk scene. This subsequently influenced American antifa movements in the late 1980s and 1990s, which grew significantly in the 21st century to counter the radical right.

Anti-fascism encompasses political movements united in their opposition to fascist ideologies, organizations, and individuals. Initiated in Europe during the 1920s, the movement attained its historical zenith shortly before and during World War II, wherein the Axis powers were contested by an international coalition of allied nations and numerous clandestine resistance networks.
pages.caption: Hitler with Mussolini at the site of the 20 July Plot, an attempted bombing assassination of Hitler by dissident German military officers that took place in 1944

pages.text: Prior to World War II, Western powers frequently underestimated the fascist threat, occasionally conflating anti-fascism with communism. Nevertheless, the onset of the war dramatically recalibrated Western perspectives. Consequently, fascism was reinterpreted as an existential peril by the Soviet Union alongside liberal democracies such as the United States and the United Kingdom.
pages.caption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

evidence.fileTitle: File:FDR-1944-Campaign-Portrait (retouched, cropped) (1).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

pages.text: Initial anti-fascist mobilizations materialized in Italy amid Benito Mussolini's ascendancy, subsequently proliferating across Europe and internationally. This nascent phase incorporated communist, socialist, anarchist, and Christian-democratic intellectuals. Crucially, until the conclusion of the united front period in 1928, substantive collaboration persisted between communist and non-communist factions.
pages.caption: Winston Churchill

evidence.fileTitle: File:Sir Winston Churchill - 19086236948.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Winston Churchill

pages.text: Within Italy, Mussolini's administration co-opted the term anti-fascist to designate domestic adversaries, deploying a dedicated secret police apparatus for suppression. Throughout the 1920s, anti-fascist elements drawn from the labor movement resisted the violent Blackshirts. Following the capitulation of mainstream trade unions to legalist strategies, recalcitrant workers instituted autonomous defensive organizations such as the Arditi del Popolo.
pages.caption: Charles de Gaulle

pages.text: In the postwar era, anti-fascist activism persisted across territories where organized fascism attempted resurgence. A prominent resurgence of antifa manifested in 1980s Germany as a countermeasure to neo-Nazi infiltration of the punk subculture, subsequently catalyzing parallel movements in the United States. These networks experienced heightened prominence in the 21st century amid wider mainstream revivals of the radical right.

Anti-fascism is a political movement that opposes fascist ideologies, groups, and individuals. Originating in Europe during the 1920s, it reached its greatest significance shortly before and during World War II. During this conflict, the Axis powers were opposed by numerous allied nations and dozens of global resistance movements.

pages.text: Before World War II, Western countries largely failed to take the threat of fascism seriously, and anti-fascism was sometimes linked with communism. However, the outbreak of the war fundamentally altered Western perceptions. Fascism was suddenly viewed as an existential threat not only by the Soviet Union, but also by the democratic United States and United Kingdom.

evidence.articleCaption: Franklin D. Roosevelt

pages.text: Anti-fascist movements emerged initially in Italy during the rise of Benito Mussolini before spreading globally. The early period involved communist, socialist, anarchist, and Christian-democratic organizers. Until 1928, there was significant collaboration between communist and non-communist anti-fascists.

evidence.fileTitle: File:Sir Winston Churchill - 19086236948.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Winston Churchill

pages.text: In Italy, Mussolini's regime labeled its opponents as anti-fascists and established a secret police force for repression. Throughout the 1920s, anti-fascists fought against violent Blackshirts and Mussolini's rise. When some labor groups adopted pacified strategies, dissenting workers formed groups like Arditi del Popolo to continue the fight.

pages.text: Following World War II, the movement remained active wherever organized fascism re-emerged. A resurgence of antifa occurred in Germany during the 1980s in response to neo-Nazis infiltrating the punk scene. This subsequently influenced American antifa movements in the late 1980s and 1990s, which grew significantly in the 21st century to counter the radical right.

pages.text: A trade route is a path used to move cargo between places. Ancient routes helped people share goods, ideas, and cultures across the world. They connected distant markets with long paths and smaller roads.

evidence.articleCaption: Map of Central Asia with its trade routes and movements between 128 BCE to 150 CE

pages.text: Long-distance trade started long ago in the Chalcolithic period. Societies in Asia, Europe, and the Mediterranean built major networks to move items. Animals and portage helped make this travel possible.
pages.caption: A Javanese jong, a large Javanese vessel from the 11th−17th century. Shown with the characteristic tanja sail of Southeast Asian Austronesians.

pages.text: Caravans carried luxury goods across large distances. Camels helped nomads control the spice and silk trade from the East. Transporting cheap goods was not profitable for these caravan operators.
pages.caption: For centuries, the Grand Trunk Road has served as the main artery for travel across Northern India. A scene from the Ambala cantonment during the days of the British Raj.

pages.text: Water travel was also very important for early trade. The Egyptians used Red Sea routes to bring spices from East Africa and Arabia. Romans built hard highways using concrete made from volcanic ash.

pages.text: In modern times, commercial activity shifted to new routes between countries. People started using trains, automobiles, and cargo airplanes. Pipelines were also built to transport oil and natural gas safely.

A trade route serves as a logistical network of pathways and stoppages designed for the commercial transport of cargo. pages.text: Trade routes constitute logistical frameworks comprising pathways and stoppages dedicated to the commercial transit of cargo. Historically, long-distance networks facilitated the exchange of material goods, cultural practices, and technological innovations across civilizations, linking primary commercial arteries with secondary distribution networks.

pages.text: The genesis of long-distance trade routes dates to the Chalcolithic period. By the middle of the second millennium BCE, prominent societies across the Mediterranean, Mesopotamia, South Asia, and China engineered extensive transportation networks, heavily reliant on portage and the domestication of beasts of burden.
pages.caption: A Javanese jong, a large Javanese vessel from the 11th−17th century. Shown with the characteristic tanja sail of Southeast Asian Austronesians.

pages.text: Organized caravans specialized in transporting high-value luxury commodities, as low-value goods were economically unviable for overland transit. Concurrently, maritime navigation developed from coastal cabotage to pelagic voyages exploiting monsoon wind patterns, drastically reducing transport costs relative to overland alternatives.

pages.text: Architectural and infrastructural advancements characterized regional networks, exemplified by Roman concrete highways constructed from volcanic ash and lime. Urban trading networks expanded along the Persian Gulf and eastern Mediterranean, generating an interdependent world system of interacting civilizations with distinct regional foci.

title: The Multinational Force in Lebanon
attribution: Adapted from English Wikipedia contributors; see pinned revision and history. SAGA AI-assisted adaptation under CC BY-SA 4.0. Wikipedia does not endorse SAGA.

pages.text: In August 1982, countries made a new peacekeeping group called the Multinational Force in Lebanon. They wanted to help stop fighting and help people leave safely after a big conflict involving Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization.
pages.caption: Commission for Philip Habib for his trip as Special Representative of the President of the United States for the Middle East in 1982, signed by President Ronald Reagan and Secretary of State George P. Shultz

evidence.fileTitle: File:PhilipHabibMiddleEastCommission.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Commission for Philip Habib for his trip as Special Representative of the President of the United States for the Middle East in 1982, signed by President Ronald Reagan and Secretary of State George P. Shultz

pages.text: Four countries joined to help. These countries were the United States, France, Italy, and Britain. Their main job was to oversee a peaceful withdrawal and to train units of the local Lebanese Armed Forces.
pages.caption: The United States Marine Corps barracks in Beirut, 1982

imageProvenance.credit: James Case from Philadelphia, Mississippi, U.S.A.

evidence.fileTitle: File:Marine Barracks, Beirut 1982.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: The United States Marine Corps barracks in Beirut, 1982

pages.text: The French Armed Forces landed in Beirut on August 21, and the U.S. Marines arrived on August 25. The Italian Armed Forces arrived on August 26. This initial force was tasked with securing Beirut's port through which fighters would be evacuated by ship.
pages.caption: U.S. Navy Amphibian arriving in Beirut, 1982

imageProvenance.credit: James Case from Philadelphia, Mississippi, U.S.A.

evidence.fileTitle: File:Navy Amphibian, Beirut 1982.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: U.S. Navy Amphibian arriving in Beirut, 1982

pages.text: Later, the situation changed and became very dangerous due to renewed civil war and tragic attacks. The peacekeeping mission faced severe violence, including a terrible bombing that killed many servicemen.
pages.caption: U.S. Marines of the 32d Marine Amphibious Unit and legionnaires of the 2nd Foreign Parachute Regiment form a joint security guard during the evacuation of the PLO from Beirut, Lebanon.

imageProvenance.credit: Photo courtesy Maj Fred T. Lash, USMC (Ret)

evidence.fileTitle: File:USMC-Lebanon82-12.jpg
evidence.articleCaption: U.S. Marines of the 32d Marine Amphibious Unit and legionnaires of the 2nd Foreign Parachute Regiment form a joint security guard during the evacuation of the PLO from Beirut, Lebanon.

pages.text: The early peaceful environment ended as the civil war re-escalated after the assassination of President-elect Bashir Gemayel in September 1982. The international force ended its mission and went offshore before completely leaving Lebanon in July 1984 in the aftermath of the October 1983 barracks bombing that killed 241 U.S. and 58 French servicemen.

The Multinational Force was established in August 1982 following a ceasefire mediated by the United States between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization. Its original purpose was to assist the Lebanese Armed Forces in safely evacuating the PLO and other foreign combatants from Beirut.
pages.caption: Commission for Philip Habib for his trip as Special Representative of the President of the United States for the Middle East in 1982, signed by President Ronald Reagan and Secretary of State George P. Shultz

pages.text: This four-nation mission included military units from the United States, France, Italy, and later Britain. Beyond overseeing the withdrawal, the force was tasked with training the Lebanese Armed Forces and promoting national reconciliation.

This initial force of U.S., French, and Italian troops was tasked with securing Beirut's port through which the Palestine Liberation Organization would be evacuated by ship. The next morning, the first ship arrived to begin evacuating forces.

pages.text: However, the environment deteriorated sharply after political assassinations reignited the civil war. The force increasingly became viewed as a participant rather than a neutral peacekeeper amid escalating hostilities.

pages.text: Following a devastating October 1983 barracks bombing that caused numerous casualties among U.S. and French personnel, the mission became untenable. The international forces withdrew offshore before completely leaving Lebanon in July 1984.

Constituted in August 1982 in the wake of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire between Israel and the PLO, the Multinational Force aimed to facilitate the departure of foreign combatants and assist the Lebanese Armed Forces during a critical juncture of the civil war.

B1-B2.headline: The History and Impact of Social Movements

pages.text: A social movement is a loosely organized effort by a large number of people to achieve a specific goal, typically social or political. These movements can promote social change or resist it, acting as a method of bottom-up change within nations. While many aim for equality, others seek to maintain existing power relationships.

C1-C2.headline: Dynamics and Theories of Social Movements

pages.text: Social movements constitute loosely organized collective efforts by large populations aiming to achieve specific social or political objectives. These groups can instigate structural transformations or alternatively resist them, functioning as endogenous mechanisms of political and social change from within nations.

pages.text: Scholars such as Mario Diani argue that definitions of social movements generally share three core criteria: a network of informal interactions among individuals, groups, or organizations engaged in political or cultural conflict based on a shared collective identity. Other theorists like Charles Tilly and Sidney Tarrow emphasize sustained interactions and collective challenges against elites.

pages.text: The historical genesis of modern social movements is frequently attributed to 19th-century industrialization, urbanization, and the broader dissemination of literature. Urban environments facilitated dense social networks where working populations could congregate, addressing shared grievances regarding economic wellbeing and political rights.

pages.text: Theoretical frameworks examining movement emergence encompass resource mobilization theory, which stresses the necessity of internal and external resources like funding and legitimacy, and political process theory, which emphasizes insurgent consciousness, organizational strength, and political opportunities. Additionally, framing perspectives incorporate cultural and psychological dimensions, addressing shared ideologies and the free-rider problem.
